# SkePU-BLAS API {#sec-skepublas}

This appendix chapter documents the SkePU-BLAS coverage and API
interface as in [@Ernstsson2022PhD]. The SkePU-BLAS coverage is level-1
BLAS and the dense (full storage) operations from level 2 and 3,
including those of symmetric, Hermitian and triangular matrices (which
are stored in a triangle of a full `Matrix`). The banded and packed
storage formats are not supported, and their functions are omitted below.

SkePU-BLAS replaces the character arguments in CBLAS with C++-style
type-safe `enum`s:

    enum class Op : char { NoTrans = 'N', Trans = 'T', ConjTrans = 'C' }; 

The following subsections contain the complete API specification for
SkePU-BLAS, showing equivalence to one or several CBLAS functions in
each case.

All SkePU-BLAS functions below are namespaced under `skepu::blas`, and
signatures are defined in header `skepu-lib/blas`.

An example of using SkePU-BLAS, Conjugate Gradient computing, is given
in @sec-CG.

## Conventions {#sec-skepublas-conventions}

**Vectors.** A routine on $n$ elements of a vector `x` with the
increment `incx` works on the elements `x[0]`, `x[incx]`, ...,
`x[(n-1) * incx]` of the `Vector`, which can be longer than that (it
needs at least $1 + (n-1)|incx|$ elements, which is checked). A
negative increment starts from the far end, as in the reference BLAS:
the first element of the operation is `x[(n-1) * |incx|]`. The routines
that are not defined for a negative increment in the reference BLAS
(`scal`, `nrm2`, `asum`, `iamax`) do nothing, or give zero, for one.
Strided and reversed vectors are handled by the skeletons (a stride), or
by a copy of the elements when a stride cannot be used.

**Matrices.** The matrices are row-major SkePU `Matrix` containers, which
carry their own leading dimension: the `lda`, `ldb` and `ldc` arguments
must be the number of columns of the `Matrix` (an error otherwise). A
routine on $m \times n$ elements works on the leading $m \times n$ part of
the matrix, which is all of it for a matrix of that size.

**Zero sizes and not-a-number.** A routine with a size of zero does
nothing, and a scalar result is zero. As in the reference BLAS, the terms
of a product are not read if `alpha` is zero, and the old value of the
result is not read if `beta` is zero (so that a not-a-number in them does
not go to the result). `iamax` returns a zero-based index, the first one
of equal values, and zero for no elements.

## Level 0 BLAS Functions

### Setup Givens rotation: `rotg`

CBLAS functions: SROTG, DROTG, CROTG, ZROTG

SkePU-BLAS signature:

```cpp
template<typename T>
void rotg (T *a, T *b, T *c, T *s)
```

### Apply Givens rotation: `rot`

CBLAS functions: SROT, DROT, CSROT, ZDROT

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TX, TY>>
void rot (
 size_type n,
 Vector<TX> & x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy,
 TS c,
 TS s
)
```

### Setup modified Givens rotation: `rotmg`

CBLAS functions: SROTMG, DROTMG

```cpp
template<typename T>
void rotmg (T *d1, T *d2, T *x1, T y1, T *param)
```

`param` has five elements: the flag and the elements `H11`, `H21`,
`H12` and `H22` of the transformation, as in the reference BLAS (the
elements that the flag says are 1, -1 or 0 are not set).

### Apply modified Givens rotation: `rotm`

CBLAS functions: SROTM, DROTM

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TX, TY>>
void rotm (
 size_type n,
 Vector<TX> & x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy,
 const TS * param
)
```

### Swap x and y: `swap`

CBLAS functions: SSWAP, DSWAP, CSWAP, ZSWAP

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY>
void swap (
 size_type n,
 Vector<TX> & x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

## Level 1 BLAS Functions

### Vector scaling: `scal`

$x := a * x$

CBLAS functions: SSCAL, DSCAL, CSSCAL, CSCAL

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TS>
void scal (
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> & x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

### Vector copy: `copy`

$y := x$

CBLAS functions: SCOPY, DCOPY, CCOPY, ZCOPY

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY>
 void copy (
 size_type n,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

### AXPY: `axpy`

$y := a * x + y$

CBLAS functions: SAXPY, CAXPY, DAXPY, ZAXPY

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TX, TY>>
void axpy (
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

### Dot product: `dot`

CBLAS functions: SDOT, DDOT, CDOTC, ZDOTC

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY>
Scalar<scalar_type<TX, TY>> dot (
 size_type n,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

### Dot product with extended precision: `dsdot`, `sdsdot`

CBLAS functions: DSDOT, SDSDOT

```cpp
Scalar<double> dsdot (
 size_type n,
 Vector<float> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<float> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy
)

Scalar<float> sdsdot (
 size_type n,
 float sb,
 Vector<float> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<float> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

The products and the sum are in double precision. `sdsdot` adds `sb`
to the dot product and rounds the result to `float`. (Not for the OpenCL
backend, on devices that do not have double precision.)

### Dot product: `dotu`

CBLAS functions: CDOTU, ZDOTU

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY>
Scalar<scalar_type<TX, TY>> dotu (
 size_type n,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

### Euclidian norm: `nrm2`

CBLAS functions: SNRM2, DNRM2, SCNRM2, DZNRM2

```cpp
template<typename T>
Scalar<real_type<T>> nrm2 (
 size_type n,
 Vector<T> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

### Sum of absolute values: `asum`

CBLAS functions: SASUM, DASUM, SCASUM, DZASUM

```cpp
template<typename T>
Scalar<real_type<T>> asum (
 size_type n,
 Vector<T> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

### Index of maximum absolute value: `iamax`

CBLAS functions: ISAMAX, IDAMAX, ICAMAX, IZAMAX

```cpp
template<typename T>
size_type iamax (
 size_type n,
 Vector<T> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

### Index of minimum absolute value: `iamin`

CBLAS functions: ISAMIN, IDAMIN, ICAMIN, IZAMIN

```cpp
template<typename T>
size_type iamin (
 size_type n,
 Vector<T> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

### Scaled vector sum: `axpby`

$y := a * x + b * y$

CBLAS functions: SAXPBY, DAXPBY, CAXPBY, ZAXPBY

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TX, TY>>
void axpby (
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 TS beta,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

## Level 2 BLAS Functions

### Matrix-vector multiply: `gemv`

CBLAS functions: SGEMV, DGEMV, CGEMV, ZGEMV

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TX, typename TY,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TX, TY>>
void gemv(
 blas::Op
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 TS beta,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

### Rank-1 update: `ger`

CBLAS functions: SGER, DGER, CGERC, ZGERC

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY, typename TA,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TX, TY>>
void ger (
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy,
 Matrix<TA> & A,
 stride_type lda
)
```

### Rank-1 update: `geru`

CBLAS functions: GCERU, ZGERU

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TY, typename TA,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TX, TY>>
void geru (
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy,
 Matrix<TA> & A,
 stride_type lda
)
```

### Symmetric and Hermitian matrix-vector multiply: `symv`, `hemv`

$y := a * A * x + b * y$

CBLAS functions: SSYMV, DSYMV, CHEMV, ZHEMV

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TX, typename TY,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TX, TY>>
void symv (  // and hemv
 Uplo uplo,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 TS beta,
 Vector<TY> & y,
 stride_type incy
)
```

The matrix is the one that the `uplo` triangle of `A` stands for (the other
triangle is not read): `A` is symmetric for `symv`, and Hermitian for `hemv`
(with a real diagonal).

### Triangular matrix-vector multiply: `trmv`

$x := op(A) * x$

CBLAS functions: STRMV, DTRMV, CTRMV, ZTRMV

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TX>
void trmv (
 Uplo uplo,
 Op trans,
 Diag diag,
 size_type n,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Vector<TX> & x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

### Triangular solve: `trsv`

Solves $op(A) * x = b$, where `x` holds $b$ and is replaced by the solution.

CBLAS functions: STRSV, DTRSV, CTRSV, ZTRSV

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TX>
void trsv (
 Uplo uplo,
 Op trans,
 Diag diag,
 size_type n,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Vector<TX> & x,
 stride_type incx
)
```

A substitution is sequential: it is done in `n` steps, one Map for each
element of the solution (the elements that are solved for are as they were).
It is correct on all backends, but with a latency for each step that makes it
slow for large `n`.

### Symmetric and Hermitian rank-1 and rank-2 update: `syr`, `her`, `syr2`, `her2`

$A := A + a * x * x^T$ (`syr`), $A := A + a * x * x^H$ (`her`, with a real $a$),
$A := A + a * (x * y^T + y * x^T)$ (`syr2`),
$A := A + a * x * y^H + \overline{a} * y * x^H$ (`her2`)

CBLAS functions: SSYR, DSYR, CHER, ZHER, SSYR2, DSYR2, CHER2, ZHER2

```cpp
template<typename TX, typename TA, typename TS>
void syr (  // and her
 Uplo uplo,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Matrix<TA> & A,
 size_type lda
)

template<typename TX, typename TY, typename TA, typename TS>
void syr2 (  // and her2
 Uplo uplo,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Vector<TX> BLAS_CONST& x,
 stride_type incx,
 Vector<TY> BLAS_CONST& y,
 stride_type incy,
 Matrix<TA> & A,
 size_type lda
)
```

Only the `uplo` triangle of `A` is updated.

## Level 3 BLAS Functions

### Matrix-matrix multiply: `gemm`

CBLAS functions: SGEMM, DGEMM, CGEMM, ZGEMM

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TB, typename TC>
void gemm (
 blas::Op transA,
 blas::Op transB,
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 size_type k,
 scalar_type<TA, TB, TC> alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Matrix<TB> BLAS_CONST& B,
 size_type ldb,
 scalar_type<TA, TB, TC> beta,
 Matrix<TC>& C,
 size_type ldc
)
```

### Symmetric and Hermitian matrix-matrix multiply: `symm`, `hemm`

$C := a * A * B + b * C$ (`side` is `Left`) or $C := a * B * A + b * C$ (`Right`)

CBLAS functions: SSYMM, DSYMM, CSYMM, ZSYMM, CHEMM, ZHEMM

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TB, typename TC,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TB, TC>>
void symm (  // and hemm
 Side side,
 Uplo uplo,
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Matrix<TB> BLAS_CONST& B,
 size_type ldb,
 TS beta,
 Matrix<TC> & C,
 size_type ldc
)
```

### Rank-k and rank-2k update: `syrk`, `herk`, `syr2k`, `her2k`

$C := a * A * A^T + b * C$ (`syrk`, with $A^T * A$ for `trans` not `NoTrans`),
$C := a * A * A^H + b * C$ (`herk`), $C := a * (A * B^T + B * A^T) + b * C$ (`syr2k`),
$C := a * A * B^H + \overline{a} * B * A^H + b * C$ (`her2k`)

CBLAS functions: SSYRK, DSYRK, CSYRK, ZSYRK, CHERK, ZHERK, SSYR2K, DSYR2K,
CSYR2K, ZSYR2K, CHER2K, ZHER2K

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TC, typename TS>
void syrk (  // and herk (trans is NoTrans or ConjTrans, alpha and beta are real)
 Uplo uplo,
 Op trans,
 size_type n,
 size_type k,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 TS beta,
 Matrix<TC> & C,
 size_type ldc
)

template<typename TA, typename TB, typename TC, typename TS>
void syr2k (  // and her2k (beta is real)
 Uplo uplo,
 Op trans,
 size_type n,
 size_type k,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Matrix<TB> BLAS_CONST& B,
 size_type ldb,
 TS beta,
 Matrix<TC> & C,
 size_type ldc
)
```

Only the `uplo` triangle of `C` is updated.

### Triangular matrix-matrix multiply: `trmm`

$B := a * op(A) * B$ (`side` is `Left`) or $B := a * B * op(A)$ (`Right`)

CBLAS functions: STRMM, DTRMM, CTRMM, ZTRMM

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TB,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TB>>
void trmm (
 Side side,
 Uplo uplo,
 Op trans,
 Diag diag,
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Matrix<TB> & B,
 size_type ldb
)
```

### Triangular solve with multiple right-hand sides: `trsm`

Solves $op(A) * X = a * B$ (`Left`) or $X * op(A) = a * B$ (`Right`) for $X$, which replaces $B$.

CBLAS functions: STRSM, DTRSM, CTRSM, ZTRSM

```cpp
template<typename TA, typename TB,
         typename TS = scalar_type<TA, TB>>
void trsm (
 Side side,
 Uplo uplo,
 Op trans,
 Diag diag,
 size_type m,
 size_type n,
 TS alpha,
 Matrix<TA> BLAS_CONST& A,
 size_type lda,
 Matrix<TB> & B,
 size_type ldb
)
```

As `trsv`, this is a substitution with one Map for each row (`Left`) or
column (`Right`) of the solution. The Map of a step works on all the
right-hand sides at once.

## Example: Conjugate-Gradient Solver {#sec-CG}

The following example code using SkePU-BLAS functions is adapted from
[@Ernstsson2022PhD].

```cpp
#include <skepu>
#include <skepu-lib/io.hpp>
#include <skepu-lib/blas.hpp>

template<typename T>
void conjugate_gradient(
 skepu::Matrix<T> BLAS_CONST& A,
 skepu::Vector<T> BLAS_CONST& b,
 skepu::Vector<T> &x)
{
 size_t N = b.size();
 assert(A.size_i() == N && A.size_j() == N && x.size() == N);
 skepu::Vector<T> p(N), r(N), Ap(N);
 // Set up initial r and p:
 skepu::blas::copy( N, b, 1, r, 1 );
 skepu::blas::gemv( skepu::blas::Op::NoTrans,
                    N, N, -1.f, A, N, x, 1, 1.f, r, 1 );
 skepu::blas::copy( N, r, 1, p, 1 );  // p := r
 float rTr = skepu::blas::dot( N, r, 1, r, 1 );  // rTr = r * r

 for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {

   // Compute alpha:
   skepu::blas::gemv( skepu::blas::Op::NoTrans,
                      N, N, 1.f, A, N, p, 1, 0.f, Ap, 1 );  // Ap := A * p
   float tmp = skepu::blas::dot( N, p, 1, Ap, 1 );  // tmp := p * Ap
   float alpha = rTr / tmp;

   // Update x:
   skepu::blas::axpy(N, alpha, p, 1, x, 1);  // x := x + alpha * p

   // Update r:
   skepu::blas::axpy( N, -alpha, Ap, 1, r, 1 );  // r := r - alpha * Ap

   // Compute beta:
   float rTr_new = skepu::blas::dot( N, r, 1, r, 1 );  // rTr_new  := r*r
   float beta = rTr_new / rTr;

   // Early exit condition:
   if (sqrt(rTr_new) < 1e-10f)
   return;

   // Update p:
   skepu::blas::scal( N, beta, p, 1 );  // p := beta * p
   skepu::blas::axpy( N, 1.f, r, 1, p, 1 );  // p := r + p
   rTr = rTr_new;
 }
}
```
